title: Robotics: Build a Voice-Controlled Robotic Hand
description: From a blinking LED to a 3D-printed hand whose fingers move when you say open, close or point, driven by an ESP32.

prerequisites: A Mac with a USB port
An ESP32 development board and USB data cable
No programming or electronics experience needed
teach.goal: Build a robotic hand controlled by an ESP32 that moves its fingers from voice commands.

project.name: Voice-controlled robotic hand
project.final_state: A 3D-printed hand with five servo-driven fingers, powered from its own 5 V supply, with an I2S microphone on an ESP32. A trained keyword model hears open, close and point and moves the fingers smoothly, with a cooldown so it does not twitch, and typed commands as a backup.

modules.title: Week 1: Electronics and code basics
modules.milestone: Your sketch blinks an LED and answers typed words.

modules.title: Week 2: Servos and the hand
modules.milestone: An assembled hand that opens, closes and points from code.

modules.title: Week 3: Commands and the microphone
modules.milestone: Typed words move the hand smoothly, and the microphone measures sound.

modules.title: Week 4: Voice control
modules.milestone: Saying open, close or point moves the hand.
